title: Security Assessment of the World Monitor application
dataset_link: App link- https://www.worldmonitor.app Source Code: https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor
description:
• Background The world Monitor application is a Web/ Mobile platform that provides users with real-time monitoring, analytics, and reporting features. The application handles user authentication, data visualization, API communication, and role-based access controls.
As a security analyst, the task is to evaluate the application's security posture and identify vulnerabilities that could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the system.
• Description Conduct an authorized security assessment of the World Monitor application to:
1. Identify security vulnerabilities in the application.
2. Assess the potential impact of each vulnerability.
3. Demonstrate proof-of-concept exploitation in a controlled environment.
4. Recommend remediation measures to mitigate the identified risks.
• Scope The assessment should focus on:
• Authentication and session management
• Authorization and access control
• Input validation and data handling
• API security
• Client-side security controls
• Secure communication mechanisms
• Data storage and privacy protections
• Success Criteria The assessment is considered successful if:
• At least one valid vulnerability is identified and documented.
• Evidence supports the existence of the vulnerability.
• Risk and impact are clearly explained.
• Practical mitigation strategies are provided
• Expected Solution/Deliverables:
For each vulnerability discovered, provide:
• Vulnerability title
• Description
• Affected component
• Severity rating (e.g., CVSS)
• Steps to reproduce
• Proof of concept demonstrating the issue in a safe testing environment
• Business impact assessment
• Remediation recommendations constraints
• Testing must be performed only on authorized systems.
• No actions should affect production users or data.
• Exploitation should be limited to proof-of-concept validation.
• Compliance with applicable laws, policies, and ethical hacking guidelines is required.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on api, real-time, compliance. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 16/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Security Assessment of the World Monitor Application

overview.in_plain_terms: Conduct an authorized penetration test of a real-time monitoring web/mobile application, systematically checking authentication, access control, input handling, API security, and data protection, and document findings with clear remediation guidance.
overview.why_it_matters: Applications handling real-time monitoring, analytics, and role-based access need genuine security validation before they can be trusted with sensitive operational data.
pain_points: Authentication and session management can have real, exploitable weaknesses.
Authorization/access-control flaws can let users access data or functions beyond their role.
API and client-side security is often under-tested compared to server-side logic.
overview.background: This is an authorized security assessment challenge against a named application (World Monitor), covering standard web/mobile application security domains.
overview.whats_being_asked: A structured, authorized penetration test covering authentication, authorization, input validation, API security, client-side security, secure communication, and data storage, with at least one documented, demonstrated vulnerability and remediation guidance.
expected_solution: Systematic security testing across the named scope areas.
At least one valid, documented vulnerability with proof-of-concept demonstration.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: N/A, this is a standard, methodology-driven security assessment task, evaluated on thoroughness and rigor of testing, not novel technique.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate, requires genuine, systematic application of established web/mobile security testing methodology (OWASP-style categories), real effort in thoroughness, not invention.

competitive_landscape.note: Requires genuine application security testing skill (a distinct discipline from general software development), appeals to security-focused participants specifically.

innovation.note: This is a methodology-application task, evaluated on testing rigor, not innovation.

invention.note: Uses established security testing methodology, real value is in thorough, systematic, well-documented application.

technical_feasibility.note: Achievable for a team with genuine application security testing skill within 36 hours; not achievable without it.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly validates or improves the security posture of a real application.

architecture.note: Not applicable, this is a testing and documentation deliverable, not a build.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with genuine application security testing (penetration testing) skill. Success depends entirely on real, hands-on security testing methodology applied systematically and ethically within the authorized scope.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very clear, well-defined success criteria (at least one valid, documented, demonstrated vulnerability) give a concrete, achievable target.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Without genuine application security testing skill, a team would struggle to find real, valid vulnerabilities rather than superficial or false-positive findings.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm real, hands-on web/mobile application security testing experience on your team, this PS rewards genuine testing rigor and methodology, not general software development skill.

idea_0_4: Confirm your testing is strictly within the authorized scope and environment provided for this challenge.
Plan systematic coverage across each named scope area (authentication, authorization, input validation, API security, client-side, communication, data storage).
Split testing responsibility across scope areas among team members with relevant security testing experience.
prototype_4_22: Systematically test authentication and session management (session fixation, token handling, password policies).
Test authorization/access control (privilege escalation, insecure direct object references, role-boundary violations).
Test input validation and API security (injection points, parameter tampering, API authentication).
integration_22_30: Test client-side security controls and secure communication mechanisms.
Test data storage and privacy protections.
Document each finding with reproduction steps, impact assessment, and proof-of-concept, staying within authorized scope and controlled demonstration only.
polish_30_36: Compile your findings into a clear, professional security assessment report.
Prioritize findings by severity and provide specific, actionable remediation guidance for each.
Rehearse presenting your methodology and at least one clearly demonstrated finding.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Present a genuinely valid, well-documented vulnerability with a clear, controlled proof-of-concept demonstration and specific, actionable remediation guidance, not just a list of theoretical concerns, that concrete, real finding is what the success criteria explicitly ask for.

strengths: Very clear, concrete success criteria give an achievable target.
Real, direct value in validating and improving application security.
weaknesses: Completely dependent on genuine application security testing skill, not accessible to a general software team.
Testing must stay strictly within authorized scope, this is a real ethical/legal boundary, not just a technical constraint.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: This PS requires genuine, hands-on application security testing experience, not general development skill.
team_fit.approach: Divide testing responsibility across the named scope areas among team members with relevant experience in each.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The actual security testing itself, requires real, hands-on penetration testing skill and judgment, this cannot be substituted with generic AI-generated test scripts without real understanding of what's being tested and why.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: AI-generated generic vulnerability scanning results without expert human validation and controlled demonstration would not meet the PS's success criteria of a genuinely valid, documented, demonstrated finding.

data_resource_availability.status: Testing must be conducted strictly within the authorized scope and environment explicitly provided for this challenge, never against unauthorized systems.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, only the provided authorized target should ever be tested.

judge_qna.question: Walk me through your most significant finding, how did you discover it and validate it's real?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present your specific vulnerability, discovery methodology, controlled proof-of-concept demonstration, and impact assessment in detail.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the remediation you'd recommend, and how would you verify the fix actually resolves it?

judge_qna.question: How did you ensure your testing stayed within authorized scope and didn't cause unintended impact?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe your specific testing discipline and any precautions taken to avoid disruption, this is a real professional responsibility in authorized security testing.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would you do differently in a real, production security assessment versus this controlled challenge environment?
